who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), writer lane for D162 (one pins/ folder)
what: The brief asked for one Python module that every script reads the pins through. tools/python-allowed.txt refuses any new .py file, so a fresh `pins.py` could not be added. The existing harness/toolchain_pins.py (the writer of rust.txt) became the reader too, and scripts outside harness/ reach it with sys.path. Separately, tools/ratchets/third-party.txt says `(all) 0 0 0`, but about 50 workspace members name third-party packages (libc, serde, wasmtime, zstd...). It is a written ratchet that was never rewritten, not a measurement.
cost: about ten minutes to find the allow-list; the third-party row needs a `thirdparty write` that a write-only lane cannot run
cause: the allow-list freezes file names, not concepts; the third-party list's `(all)` row was hand-set to the goal rather than written by the tool
whys: an allow-list of files makes 'add the right module' and 'add a stray script' look the same
class: a frozen list standing in for a rule
prevention: let python-allowed.txt name modules by role, or let a rename keep a row; run `thirdparty {"command": "write"}` once so the list is what the tool measures
annoyance: a write-only lane cannot rewrite a measured ratchet
workaround: reused harness/toolchain_pins.py; the third-party row is left for the main agent to rewrite
